prompt: Do a picky engineering review of the latest commit (HEAD) in the Chibi checkout at /Users/cwaldner/Personal/chibi/.worktrees/review-eval/chibi. It adds a call-site census in Chibi and a typed element count in C. Read only, don't change anything. Save the review as review.md.
assertions: The review states a minimum-work versus actual-work estimate for the change with concrete numbers (for example call sites or nodes multiplied by bytes scanned).

The review flags LineOf/ColumnOf rescanning the text from the start for every call site, gives a quantified cost (a count or operation estimate), and recommends using the row/column SnapshotNode already stores.
The review flags the per-element xstrdup/free in pin_array_count_type as needless allocation and recommends comparing in place.
The review flags the per-site strings.Concat("call:", callee) key building (allocation per site and/or the pointless prefix) as waste or a design defect.
The review flags CallSite's derivable or flag fields (offset/line/column copies or the is_dead list-membership bool) as a representation problem.
The review flags CountCallsInForest as a layer that only forwards and should be deleted.
The review sketches a concrete target shape for the census (for example sites as node indices, or derived counts) instead of only listing defects.

The review addresses comparing forest[index].kind against the string "call_expression", either as a finding or explicitly left alone with a stated reason about the forest's string-kind representation.
Architecture and performance findings come before correctness or bug findings in the review's ordering, or bugs are kept in a clearly separate secondary section.
Every performance finding states the work removed or its scale (a count, an estimate or a measurement).
The review does not recommend SIMD, threading or micro-optimizations (unrolling, branch hints) for this code.
The review does not recommend splitting functions for length or adding defensive NULL checks.
